main_body: Wooden coal bin: an open-top box with a dark coal mound heaped inside, a thin light wood rim, and a brown plank front face below, set on a grey checker floor.
top_band: Light tan rim at rows ~6-9 on the sides and a thin tan front rim at row ~10. The center column shows black coal from rows ~3-9, then a 1-2 row tan front rim, then the front face. There is no distinct top band of consistent height.
evidence: The bin shows its interior as a dark recess with a coal heap that rises above the rim, and the back/side rims are visible as thin tan lines. The front rim is only 1-2 rows and the opening reads as a dark cavity rather than an ellipse. A thin dark line sits under the front rim, then a plank front face of about 5 rows with a plank grid. The interior is visible from above, so it reads as an open container, but the top surface (rim) is thin. The coal mound gives a clear view into the opening, so I accept it as 3/4, although it is borderline on the rim thickness.

style.evidence: The bin uses dark brown outlines tinted to wood, with a 3-4 step wood ramp (tan rim, mid brown, dark brown planks). The coal mound is mostly a flat near-black fill of about 6x5 px with only a few lighter dots, so it counts as a flat fill. The wood front has some plank lines and variation but is thinner than the stall and well references, which carry 5-6 steps and rich tile texture. It sits slightly below the reference in density and shading.
